name: Albigensian Crusade
summary: Pope Innocent III launches the Albigensian Crusade (1209–1229) against the Cathar heresy in southern France (Languedoc), killing Simon de Montfort's famous statement at the siege of Béziers: 'Kill them all, God will know his own.' Estimates of 7,000–20,000 civilians massacred in the city. The 20-year campaign systematically destroys Occitanian culture, establishes the Papal Inquisition (1233) as a permanent institution, and transfers the County of Toulouse to the French crown (1271). It is the first crusade against fellow Christians.

_quarry.structural_significance: Destroys the distinctive Occitanian culture; establishes the Papal Inquisition; integrates Languedoc into the French royal domain; demonstrates the papacy's willingness to use crusade ideology against internal enemies
